headline: Revenue -3.7% (-7% cc) as MK Americas falls 12%; adjusted EPS $0.22 beats; Capri guides FY27 to growth and ~$2.15 EPS.
guidance_note: Initiated FY27: revenue ~ $3.525B (low-single-digit growth), adjusted EPS ~ $2.15 (~+40%); Q1 outlook softer than expected.
key_messages: Michael Kors revenue -5.5% (-8.4% cc) to $656M; Americas -12%, mainly from quality-of-sale initiatives (less discounting).
MK gross margin 64.6% vs 58.6%, helped by a $38M IEEPA tariff-refund receivable booked against cost of goods sold.
Jimmy Choo +5.3% reported, flat in constant currency, to $140M.
Adjusted operating margin -0.1% (GAAP -3.4%); GAAP loss of $0.01 per share.

consumer.big_ticket: MK demand in the Americas down double digits as the brand cuts promotions.
consumer.pricing: Reduced promotions; expected refund of IEEPA tariffs boosted margins.

macro_read: The mid-priced handbag brand keeps shrinking in the US as it cuts discounts. The tariff refund is a one-time margin boost, not a sign of better demand.
notes: Growth is as reported; Capri gives no constant-currency figure for the Americas. Versace was sold to Prada in December 2025; Jimmy Choo is still part of Capri.
$38M IEEPA tariff-refund receivable reduced MK cost of goods sold; whether adjusted EPS excludes it was not confirmed, so no EPS excluding them is shown.
Continuing operations exclude Versace (sold Dec 2025); Jimmy Choo still included.
Revenue missed consensus (Zacks) but the figure was not found; shares fell >6% intraday, close not confirmed, so null.
Company-wide gross margin change not found (MK-only +600 bps incl. tariff refund).
